text: Hey man, you see my biography here that's attached? I need you to make an adjustment to it that I guess got lost somewhere in translation. We never did a standby or a scenario actively, like moulage and shit on the highway. This was the first threat model disaster scenario I ever mapped out. When I first got invited onto the disaster team, they wanted to test my abilities, my mindset and logic. I'll upload another document. It was an earlier version that details it pretty well. What I did was essentially combine the concept of the McVeigh Oklahoma City bombing with the knowledge of Squaw Creek being 45 miles southwest of the intersection that I planned the event for. That was the threat model I built. I constructed a new one today with you, so I want to get my biography right first. But there is no motherfucker in their right goddamn sane mind on Earth that would let us shut down that freeway intersection for any amount of time other than an actual active life or death situation.

I’ll correct the biography itself, using the earlier account to preserve the distinction between a paper threat model and a live exercise. I’ll also keep the 2007 scenario separate from the threat model we developed today and check the revised document’s layout.

doc = Document(source)

body_training = next(p for p in doc.paragraphs if p.text.startswith('Hanson’s record also includes rebuilding and leading a scenario-based clinical education program'))
body_scenario = next(p for p in doc.paragraphs if p.text.startswith('A 2007 mass-casualty exercise preserved in the lineage record'))

body_training.runs[0].text = (
    'Hanson’s record includes rebuilding and leading hands-on, scenario-based clinical '
    'education focused on stress exposure and measurable performance. Separately, his '

)
body_training.runs[1].text = '  [Documented training role; named firsthand recollection for distinction]'

body_scenario.runs[0].text = (
    'When first invited onto MedStar’s Disaster Preparedness Committee (dated 2007 in the '
    'earlier lineage record), Hanson was asked to build his first disaster threat model as a '
    'test of analytical ability, mindset, and logic. His hypothetical I-820/I-35W interchange '
    'scenario combined the conceptual precedent of Timothy McVeigh’s Oklahoma City bombing '

    'It was a conceptual cascading-failure assessment, never a live field exercise: no '
    'highway standby, freeway closure, moulage, staged highway incident, or deployment occurred.'
)
body_scenario.runs[1].text = '  [Named firsthand recollection; corrected October 27, 2026]'

# Record status and original preparation date remain distinct.
assert doc.tables[0].cell(1, 1).text == 'October 3, 2026'
status_run = doc.tables[0].cell(2, 1).paragraphs[0].runs[0]
status_run.text = 'Working biographical record, v1.2; corrected October 27, 2026; evidence classes retained'

# Update firsthand source lineage with the correction, and add the supplied earlier statement.
source7 = next(p for p in doc.paragraphs if p.text.startswith('7. Firsthand recollections supplied by Hanson'))
source7.runs[0].text = (
    '7. Firsthand recollections supplied by Hanson in 2026 GMRI archival interviews and '
    'conversations, including the 2006 hiring sequence, Lisa Bennett’s intervention and '
    'later voting-history statement, the 2008 paramedic cohort, 2009 MIH discussions, and '
    'the disability hearing. Includes Hanson’s October 27, 2026 correction identifying '
    'the early I-820/I-35W disaster scenario as an unexecuted conceptual threat model, '
    'with the Oklahoma City bombing and Squaw Creek as inputs. These accounts remain '
    'firsthand recollection unless independently documented.'
)

archival_heading = next(p for p in doc.paragraphs if p.text.strip() == 'Archival note')
source8 = doc.add_paragraph(style=source7.style)
source8.paragraph_format.left_indent = source7.paragraph_format.left_indent
source8.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = source7.paragraph_format.first_line_indent
source8.add_run(
    '8. Hanson, The Clinical Audit: Systems Red-Teaming and the Preventability Standard '
    '(earlier first-person GMRI statement, PDF supplied October 27, 2026), Section 4. '
    'Distinguishes hands-on clinical training from Disaster Preparedness Committee '
    'scenario design and describes an iced-over-highway threat model. It does not '
    'document a live I-820/I-35W highway exercise or independently establish that the '
    'iced-highway and Oklahoma City/Squaw Creek models were the same design.'
)
archival_heading._p.addprevious(source8._p)

correction_heading = doc.add_paragraph('Correction to prior record (October 27, 2026)', style='Heading 2')
archival_heading._p.addprevious(correction_heading._p)

correction_body = doc.add_paragraph(style='Normal')
correction_body.add_run(
    'Version 1.1 described the 2007 I-820/I-35W material as a “mass-casualty exercise” '
    'and a “dirty-bomb scenario.” The first term incorrectly suggests a live exercise; '
    'the second did not preserve Hanson’s stated Oklahoma City bombing/Squaw Creek '
    'design inputs. In this revision, the scenario is recorded as a hypothetical threat '
    'model, not a highway operation. The correction does not reclassify his separate '
    'hands-on clinical training exercises.'
)
archival_heading._p.addprevious(correction_body._p)

# Preserve other sections and original documentary photo exhibits.
doc.core_properties.subject = 'GMRI archival biographical record — corrected disaster-preparedness threat model account'
doc.core_properties.comments = 'v1.2 source correction of MedStar Disaster Preparedness Committee threat-model description on 2026-10-27.'
doc.save(target)

check = Document(target)
combined = '\n'.join(p.text for p in check.paragraphs)

assert 'no highway standby, freeway closure, moulage' in combined
assert 'Named firsthand recollection; corrected October 27, 2026' in combined
assert 'A 2007 mass-casualty exercise preserved' not in combined
assert len(check.inline_shapes) == 2
print('Saved:', target)
print('Paragraphs:', len(check.paragraphs), 'inline exhibits:', len(check.inline_shapes), 'tables:', len(check.tables))
for p in check.paragraphs:
